key_insight: A transfer learning–based nnU-Net achieved the strongest intracranial artery segmentation and closest agreement with manual-reference hemodynamic measurements among three models tested.
clinical_relevance: Automated segmentation could reduce manual workload for 7T 4D Flow MRI research, but model choice can affect measured blood flow and wall shear stress.
method: Pretrained a 3D full-resolution nnU-Net on 355 TOF-MRA scans and fine-tuned it on 11 7T 4D Flow MRI scans.
Compared it with a direct-transfer U-Net and a DenseNet U-Net trained from scratch.
Evaluated segmentation and downstream hemodynamic measurements against manual references across test sets with different resolutions.
evidence_signal: The nnU-Net achieved Dice >0.85, HD95 approximately 3 mm, and wall shear stress ICCs of 0.96–0.97 with bias ≤1.7%.
watch_item: Only 11 7T scans were used for fine-tuning, and agreement varied by vessel, warranting broader validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Automated Segmentation of Intracranial Arteries on 4D Flow MRI for Hemodynamic Quantification
